Run meta-analysis across per-study DE results

Source: R/04_meta.R
mx_meta.Rd

Integrates per-study differential expression results from mx_de_all into a single gene-level meta-analysis. Two families of methods are available: effect-size models, which pool the per-study log2 fold changes weighted by their sampling variance, and p-value combination methods, which combine per-study evidence without pooling effects.

Usage

mx_meta(
  de_results,
  method = c("random_effects", "fixed_effects", "fisher", "stouffer", "inverse_normal",
    "minp", "maxp", "rop", "awmeta"),
  min_studies = 2,
  tau_method = c("REML", "PM", "DL"),
  hksj = FALSE,
  directional = TRUE,
  weights = NULL,
  r = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  n_samples = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

de_results

A named list of data.frame objects (the de_result slots produced by mx_de), or a named list of metaXpressStudy objects after mx_de_all. Required columns: gene_id, log2FC, pvalue, padj; effect-size methods also need lfcSE.

method

Character scalar. One of:

"random_effects"

(default) Inverse-variance random-effects model; between-study variance \(\tau^2\) estimated by tau_method. Estimates the average effect across populations and reports a prediction interval.

"fixed_effects"

Inverse-variance common-effect model. Appropriate only when studies are near-replicates (low \(I^2\)).

"fisher"

Fisher's sum of \(-2\log p\). With directional = TRUE (default) the two one-sided Fisher tests are computed and combined as in Owen (2009), so evidence in opposite directions does not accumulate. Like all Fisher-type tests it can still be driven by one extreme study; check direction_consistency.

"stouffer"

Unweighted Stouffer Z on signed z-scores.

"inverse_normal"

Weighted inverse-normal (Stouffer) combination with weights \(\sqrt{n_s}\), as in Marot et al. (2009) and Rau et al. (2014).

"minp"

Tippett's minimum p: DE in at least one study. Non-directional.

"maxp"

Wilkinson's maximum p: DE in all studies. Non-directional.

"rop"

r-th ordered p-value (Song & Tseng 2014): DE in at least r studies. Non-directional.

"awmeta"

AWmeta (Hu et al. 2026). The p-value is the adaptively weighted Fisher statistic (AW-Fisher; Li & Tseng 2011), calibrated with the AWFisher package (Huo et al. 2020), which also returns binary per-study weights indicating which studies contribute. The effect size is an REML random-effects estimate over the selected studies only (AW-REM). Requires AWFisher and lfcSE. Non-directional, as in the original method; check direction_consistency. The selected studies are reported in aw_studies.

min_studies

Integer. Minimum number of studies in which a gene must be measured. Default: 2.

tau_method

Estimator of the between-study variance for "random_effects": "REML" (default; restricted maximum likelihood), "PM" (Paule-Mandel) or "DL" (DerSimonian-Laird). REML and PM are preferred over DL, which underestimates \(\tau^2\) (Veroniki et al. 2016; Langan et al. 2019).

hksj

Logical. Apply the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment to the random-effects standard error and use a \(t_{k-1}\) reference distribution. Recommended when few studies are pooled because the standard Wald test is anti-conservative (IntHout et al. 2014). Default: FALSE.

directional

Logical. For "fisher", combine one-sided p-values in each direction (default TRUE). FALSE gives the classical Fisher test on two-sided p-values, which ignores sign.

weights

For "stouffer"-type methods and the effect estimate reported by p-value methods: NULL (default) uses per-study sample sizes from the n_case/n_control columns written by mx_de for "inverse_normal" and equal weights for "stouffer". A numeric vector (one per study) overrides this.

r

Integer. Order statistic for "rop". Default: ceiling(k / 2) for a gene measured in k studies.

alpha

Numeric. Confidence level is 1 - alpha for confidence and prediction intervals. Default: 0.05.

n_samples

Deprecated alias for weights supplied as total sample sizes; its square root is used.

...

Unused.

Value

A metaXpressResult. Its meta_table has one row per gene with columns:

gene_id

Gene identifier.

meta_log2FC, meta_se

Pooled log2 fold change and its standard error. For p-value methods this is the inverse-variance common-effect estimate, reported as a descriptive effect size.

ci_lower, ci_upper

1 - alpha confidence interval.

pi_lower, pi_upper

Random-effects prediction interval for the effect in a new study (Higgins et al. 2009); requires \(k \ge 3\).

meta_stat

Test statistic (Z, t or \(\chi^2\) as appropriate).

meta_pvalue, meta_padj

Combined p-value and its Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across genes.

tau2, i_squared, q_stat, q_pvalue

Between-study variance, \(I^2\) (%), Cochran's Q and its p-value.

n_studies, n_up, n_down

Studies measuring the gene, and those with positive / negative log2FC.

direction_consistency

Fraction of studies whose log2FC sign agrees with meta_log2FC.

Details

Use meta_padj (BH-adjusted) for significance. For a typical disease-signature meta-analysis we recommend "random_effects" with tau_method = "REML", and reporting \(I^2\) and the prediction interval alongside the pooled effect. P-value combination methods answer different questions (any vs. all vs. most studies) and should be chosen a priori, not by comparing numbers of significant genes.

A study contributes to a gene only when it reports log2FC and pvalue (plus lfcSE for effect-size methods). DESeq2 sets pvalue to NA for count outliers flagged by Cook's distance, so such genes are treated as not measured in that study. (DESeq2's independent filtering affects only padj, which is not used.)

All methods assume studies are independent. Fold-change direction must be harmonised across studies (same case/control orientation); check with mx_study_concordance.

Examples

# Three per-study results in the format written by mx_de()
set.seed(1)
genes <- paste0("G", 1:200)
de <- lapply(1:3, function(s) {
  lfc <- rnorm(200, c(rep(1, 20), rep(0, 180)), 0.3)
  se  <- runif(200, 0.2, 0.4)
  p   <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(lfc / se))
  data.frame(gene_id = genes, log2FC = lfc, lfcSE = se, pvalue = p,
             padj = p.adjust(p, "BH"), n_case = 5, n_control = 5)
})
names(de) <- c("S1", "S2", "S3")
res <- mx_meta(de, method = "random_effects", tau_method = "REML")
#> Running meta-analysis (random_effects) on 3 studies...
head(res@meta_table[order(res@meta_table$meta_pvalue), ])
